sample_unit: documents (3 corpora x 500 documents each; 294 experimental conditions)

links.outcome: Variance in retrieval performance explained by corpus, query format, and model-by-corpus interactions
links.effect: Combined context variables explained 49.0% of variance vs 47.6% for model-related effects. Model x corpus interaction eta-squared=0.040, P<.001, so model rankings shifted across corpora.
links.quote: Clinical context variables explained as much variance in retrieval performance as embedding model choice, and model × corpus interactions showed that rankings are not portable across documentation types.

links.outcome: Portability of general-domain model rankings to clinical retrieval tasks across corpora
links.effect: Model rankings shifted across corpora (model x corpus eta-squared=0.040, P<.001). Domain-specific BioBERT and ClinicalBERT performed worse than general-purpose embeddings.
links.quote: These results argue against reliance on general-domain leaderboards for clinical RAG deployment and support mandatory local validation as a methodological requirement.

unlisted_practices: Selecting embedding models for clinical RAG retrieval using corpus-specific benchmarking
Comparison of lexical (BM25) versus embedding retrieval baselines
Choice of document chunking strategy in RAG pipelines

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks retrieval configurations across clinical contexts and directly tests the deployment practice/necessity of local corpus validation vs relying on general-domain leaderboards for RAG pipeline design.

primary.practice: local validation of retrieval models across clinical corpora and query formats
